title: Wave Turbulence of Capillary Waves in Finite Systems
abstract: We consider classical problem of turbulence of capillary waves. In a series of numerical simulations it is shown that Zakharov-Filonenko spectrum corresponding to direct cascade of energy has a limited dynamic range of realization in a finite system, which shrinks with decreasing level of nonlinearity. Recent hypothesis that this dynamic range scales with average steepness as $\simμ^{8/3}$ is confirmed. As a byproduct the Zakharov-Filonenko spectrum was observed for record dynamic range close to or beyond one decade in a variety of simulation configurations.
summary: This work numerically investigates wave turbulence in capillary waves, focusing on the finite dynamic range of the Zakharov-Filonenko spectrum. The authors confirm that this dynamic range scales robustly with the nonlinearity parameter ($\mu$) as $\mu^{8/3}$. This provides a quantitative understanding of how nonlinearity limits energy cascade in finite physical systems.
main_problem: The paper investigates the wave turbulence of capillary waves in finite systems, specifically determining how the dynamic range of the Zakharov-Filonenko spectrum scales with the system's nonlinearity.
main_result: The dynamic range of the spectrum scales with the average steepness ($\mu$) according to the relationship $k_c/k_p \propto \mu^{8/3}$, which is confirmed by numerical simulations.
method: The study uses numerical simulations based on the Hamiltonian dynamics of capillary waves, analyzing the time-averaged energy spectrum to identify the inertial range and its boundaries.
model_or_system: The system is capillary waves on deep water, modeled by a weakly nonlinear expansion of the full Hamiltonian. The dynamics are governed by the Wave Kinetic Equation (WKE) derived from the coupled equations for surface elevation and velocity potential.

important_parameters: Average steepness ($\mu$), pumping wavenumber ($k_p$), and the dissipation scale ($k_d$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the nonlinearity parameter $\mu$ is small, allowing the use of the WKE, and that the turbulence is isotropic.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time-averaged, normalized energy spectra for different pumping regimes, showing the characteristic KZ spectrum and the shrinking dynamic range as $\mu$ decreases. Figure 4 specifically plots the scaling of the dynamic range versus $\mu$.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical model and the WKE, then presents numerical simulations across various pumping strengths and nonlinearity levels. The core of the work is fitting the observed scaling of the dynamic range ($k_c/k_p$) against $\mu$ to confirm the theoretical $\mu^{8/3}$ dependence.
why_interesting: The study of wave turbulence and the scaling laws derived from the WKE provide insights into non-equilibrium energy cascades, which share mathematical parallels with energy transport in complex quantum many-body systems or driven-dissipative quantum optical systems.
